subject: Proof of Erasure / Geo-fallback for Onshore Copies — DPA redline request
messages:
From: Acme Health Legal <acme.legal@acmehealth.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline — proof of erasure and onshore fallback

Hi Priyom,

Thanks for the call this morning. Our legal team is running through the DPA redlines and we need clearer language around a couple of retention/deletion items before we can sign:

1) Proof of Erasure: We need Redwood to commit to providing a certificate of erasure (signed) when customer data is deleted per the agreement (including for terminated accounts). Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a standard template that includes the deletion timestamp, scope (primary + backups), and the identity of the operator who ran the job?

2) Onshore fallback copies: For our regulated workloads we require an onshore fallback (within US) that can be used when the primary region is temporarily unavailable. We are seeing redlines that say backups may be stored "temporarily outside the region" for resilience. We need specifics: maximum duration, access controls, and an auditable process for ensuring eventual deletion/return.

3) Backup retention window: We proposed a 30-day maximum for backups after termination. Redwood’s current language leaves a longer window for disaster recovery. Are you able to accept 30 days for backups tied to deletion events, with an exception process that requires pre-approval and logging?

Please attach any sample artifacts (erase cert, example audit extract) and a proposed clause we can circulate internally.

Best,
Maya Patel
Counsel, Acme Health

--
Acme Health | Privacy & Security

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <acme.legal@acmehealth.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — proof of erasure and onshore fallback

Maya,

Appreciate the clear list — copied Laura (enterprise legal ops) and Rishi (security) so we can propose consolidated language and artifacts. High level: we can meet your intent with these practical controls and deliverables — below is our proposed compromise and the artifacts we can provide immediately.

Proposed compromise (for DPA clause):
- Proof of Erasure: Redwood will provide a signed Certificate of Erasure upon request following a deletion event (termination or customer-initiated erasure). The certificate will include deletion scope (primary storage, snapshots, and long-term backups), deletion timestamps, and the operator/process id. For backups in immutable archives, Redwood will provide an attestation of scheduling for the archive purge and evidence (audit log extract) when purged.
- Onshore fallback: Redwood may store encrypted, ephemeral fallback copies in a US onshore region for the purpose of failover during a bona fide outage. Such fallback copies will be retained only for the duration necessary to restore service resiliency and will be deleted within 14 days of the end of the outage unless otherwise agreed in writing. Access to fallback copies is restricted via role-based access controls and logged.
- Backup retention window: For customer-initiated account termination, Redwood will retain backups for a maximum of 30 days unless a documented exception is approved by Redwood’s Data Protection Officer and the customer (exceptions will be logged and visible in the audit extract).

Artifacts we can attach right now:
- Certificate of Erasure template (signed by Data Ops lead)
- Example audit log extract showing deletion job id, timestamp, and operator id
- A tracked-change DPA snippet: redwood-dpa-proposed-redlines.docx

Open items / limitations to flag:
- Immutable or escrowed archives: if data is placed into long-term immutable escrow (customer request or legal hold), purge timing may differ; we call that out explicitly in the clause.
- For very large egress requests that require multi-step migration, there may be a short operational overlap for verification — we commit to logging and minimizing that overlap.

If this looks acceptable, we’ll produce the two artifacts and a clean DocuSign packet for signature. Laura / Rishi — anything to add on the access controls or audit fields we should include in the certificate?

Thanks,
Priyom
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment stubs: redwood-dpa-proposed-redlines.docx, erase_certificate_template.pdf, audit_log_extract_example.csv

From: Maya Patel <acme.legal@acmehealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 08:29:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redline — proof of erasure and onshore fallback

Thanks Priyom — that compromise reads well and addresses our primary concerns. Two small edits from Legal:

1) The Certificate of Erasure should indicate whether the deletion affected any "derivative" datasets generated by Redwood processing pipelines (e.g., derived embeddings). If you cannot confirm derivative deletion, the certificate should state the scope explicitly.
2) For the 14-day onshore fallback window, can we add a requirement that Redwood notify customer security contacts within 24 hours of fallback activation and provide a post-incident deletion report within 7 days of fallback termination?

If you can incorporate those two lines into the DPA snippet, we can route to Procurement and sign. We will sign the DocuSign once we have the updated language and the sample Certificate.

Best,
Maya
---

Maya — thanks, and agreed on both bullets. We’ll: 
- Add explicit language about derivative datasets in the Certificate of Erasure ("scope: primary storage, snapshots, backups, and any derivative datasets generated by Redwood processing pipelines where applicable; where not applicable, certificate will state scope explicitly").
- Add the notification and post-incident reporting obligations: notify customer security contacts within 24 hours of fallback activation; provide a deletion report within 7 days of fallback termination.

Deliverables and next steps:
1) I’ve attached the edited DPA snippet (redwood-dpa-proposed-redlines.docx) with the two new sentences in tracked changes.
2) Attached is a filled example certificate (erase_certificate_template.pdf) and an audit log extract sample (audit_log_extract_example.csv) — these are template/examples for your review.
3) I’ll have Legal prepare the DocuSign packet for signature once you confirm.

We aim to ship the updated packet by EOD tomorrow. If Procurement needs a small exception form for cases where a customer requests a longer backup hold, we can include an exception workflow link.

Thanks and talk soon,
Priyom
Director, Sales Operations
Redwood Inference
